title: Ransom Canyon Canceled by Netflix
seoTitle: Netflix Cancels Ransom Canyon After Two Seasons
subtitle: The Texas romantic drama series loses its future on the platform
excerpt: Netflix has decided not to renew 'Ransom Canyon' after two seasons, despite creative adjustments made in the second season.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Netflix has opted not to renew the series "Ransom Canyon" after two seasons. The decision came after the second season recorded 4.1 million views in its first week, a 43% drop from the 7.2 million in Season 1's first week.

Why the cancellation is trending

The drop in viewership for the second season, combined with Netflix's cost-benefit analysis, led to the decision not to move forward with a third season.

How the series evolved between seasons

After the first season, the series was renewed for a second with a reduced episode count (eight episodes instead of ten) and a creative restructuring, including changes to the supporting cast.

What Netflix said about the performance

According to Netflix, the second season failed to maintain the viewership levels of the first, dropping out of the platform's Top 10 in just three weeks, compared to the first season's four-week run.

Minka Kelly's impact on the series

During the show's development, Minka Kelly requested pay equity with Josh Duhamel, which was recognized by Netflix. Although she did not achieve full parity, the request was met with near-equality.

Other shows that faced a drop in viewership

  • Running Point (-43%)
  • The Four Seasons (-63%)
  • The Gentlemen (-45%)
  • Avatar: The Last Airbender (-59%)
  • A Good Girl’s Guide to Murder (-76%)

The future of the series on Netflix

With the cancellation decision, the main characters, Staten Kirkland and Quinn O’Grady, are left without a continuation on the platform. The season two finale did not feature major cliffhangers, but it did suggest potential storylines for supporting characters.

Fan and media criticism

Some critics pointed to a lack of chemistry between the leads and questioned Netflix's strategy of casting country music stars in drama productions.

With information from Deadline.
